where: crates/blaze-scope/src/names/seam.rs (ScopeRead, RootRead) beside blaze-surface's ScopeView and CrateRootView inherent methods; met in crates/blaze-scope/src/names_cells.rs
what: With `ScopeRead`/`RootRead` in scope, `view.globs()`, `view.textual()`, `root.macro_use()` and `root.head()` pick the TRAIT method (it takes `self` by value, found before the inherent `&self` one), so the call takes other arguments or returns `Globs` instead of an iterator, and `head()` needs a type annotation for `N`. cost: three runner rounds, about two minutes
cause: the seam's methods share names with the views' inherent methods but differ in receiver and signature
whys: the seam was written to read like the views; Rust's method probe takes by-value matches first
class: a trait sharing method names but not signatures with an inherent API of the types it is implemented for
prevention: not done: rename the seam's methods (e.g. `edges`, `textual_before`, `macro_use_at`) or make the receiver `&self`; today names_cells.rs calls the inherent ones by path (`ScopeView::globs(&view)`)
annoyance: the runner hides a passing test's printed floor line (no --nocapture)
workaround: call the inherent method by its path
